text:
Thomas Baird: Heads up on metrics costs/cardinality before we roll tier/model/route everywhere. I pulled last 24h from M3 + Prom and we’re already flirting with the storage budget in us-east-1.

Current offenders (top by active series):
- `gateway_http_requests_total{route,model,region,tier,status}` (route is raw path today, includes ids)
- `runtime_token_latency_ms_bucket{model,customer,region,tier}` (customer shows up in some Dedicated envs)
- `routing_fallback_total{from_model,to_model,route,region,tier}` (pairwise explosion)

If we ship per-route/per-model/per-region + histograms, we’re going to 10–20x series. Need a plan for aggregation + sampling now.

Sergio Costa: yeah, saw this too. Grafana panels for SLO dashboards are timing out with full label sets (querying `model=*` on histogram buckets is brutal). :grimacing:

Logan Wright: +1. telemetry side: M3 series cardinality bill is linear; we can’t just “add labels” everywhere. We should define a *cardinality budget* per metric family and enforce in code review.

Allison Grant: this is basically what the observability standard doc is trying to prevent. For SLOs we need *consistent dims*, but “consistent” != “everything everywhere”. Can we align on a minimal set for SLO SLIs?

Thomas Baird: proposal v0 for SLO-related metrics:
- Required dims: `tier`, `region`, `service` (or `component`), `route_template` (not raw), `model_family` (not model_id), `status_class` (2xx/4xx/5xx/timeout)
- Optional dims behind sampling: `model_id` (top N), `route` (top N), `customer_id` (Dedicated only, restricted, not exported to shared cluster)
- Absolutely no: raw path, prompt_id, request_id, user_id, org_id

Nadia Rahman: also important: we need SLI correctness. If we aggregate too aggressively we lose ability to validate “this model is melting” vs global. But we can compromise: compute SLI numerator/denominator at ingest as counters with fixed dims, and keep high-cardinality stuff only in logs/traces.

Caleb Johnson: +1 on pushing detail to tracing/logs. For “what route is causing burn”, we can do exemplars or sampled spans tagged with model/route, rather than full metrics.

Amara Diallo: gateway side can fix the raw route issue quickly. We currently use the mux path as-is (`/v1/chat/completions/{id}` etc). We can switch to template extraction (e.g. `/v1/chat/completions`) and add `endpoint=chat.completions` instead.

Thomas Baird: awesome. That alone cuts a ton.

Sergio Costa: can we get a concrete number? like “route_template = ~30 values” vs raw path = effectively unbounded.

Thomas Baird: yep. quick back-of-napkin from yesterday:
- raw `route` distinct values: ~48k (due to customer proxies + ids)
- templated endpoints we care about: ~22 (chat/completions stream/non-stream, embeddings, rerank, catalog ops, etc)

Logan Wright: the other big one is histograms. `*_bucket` multiplies by number of buckets, so `route_template x model x region x tier x buckets` is where it explodes.

Suggestion:
1) Keep histograms only at low cardinality (service/tier/region/endpoint)
2) For per-model/per-route, emit summaries like `p95` as gauge computed offline (or use HDR histogram w/ rollup?)

Caleb Johnson: careful on “p95 gauges” computed in app. That’s super easy to get wrong + inconsistent windows. Better: keep histogram at low dims + use logs for high dims. Or compute p95 centrally in the SLO job using traces/log samples.

Nadia Rahman: +1. We already have the SLO computation job in scope (ENG-2421). That job can join:
- counters at fixed dims for availability/success
- TTFT histogram at fixed dims
- sampled spans for per-model tail analysis

Aisha Bello: from SRE/SLO standpoint we don’t need per-model histograms for the SLO itself. SLO is tier+endpoint+region. When it burns we want drill-down, but drill-down can be “top contributors” not full series.

Thomas Baird: exactly. another proposal: “topK labeling” pattern.
- Maintain a allowlist of top 20 models per tier (by traffic) updated daily.
- For model_id label, if not in allowlist => label `model_id="other"`
Same for route_template maybe top 50.

Logan Wright: telemetry can support that via a sidecar config (allowlist pushed to services). But we need a deterministic fallback so dashboards don’t break.

Sergio Costa: if we do `other`, dashboards should default to `model_family` anyway. For drilldowns we can show “other” as a bucket.

Allison Grant: can we codify this as “Cardinality Tiering”:
- Tier 0 metrics (always on): SLO metrics, low dims
- Tier 1 (sampled): drilldown metrics at 1% sampling, or allowlisted dims
- Tier 2 (debug): logs/traces only

Thomas Baird: yes. and we should add a CI check to catch new labels / exploding values (ENG-2424-ish). Something like: parse emitted metric descriptors + denylist labels.

Caleb Johnson: I can add a lint in the metrics ingestion repo too. But app-side is better.

Amara Diallo: gateway code change is straightforward. here’s what it would look like in our middleware:
```go
// before: route = r.URL.Path
// after:
routeTemplate := mux.CurrentRoute(r).GetName() // or GetPathTemplate()
labels := prometheus.Labels{
  "endpoint": routeTemplate,
  "tier": tier,
  "region": region,
  "status_class": classify(code),
}
reqs.With(labels).Inc()
```
If route template missing, we set `endpoint="unknown"` and increment a counter.

Nadia Rahman: pls also make sure streaming endpoints split TTFT vs full duration. That’s another place we saw “latency” queries go sideways.

Sergio Costa: on dashboards I’ll update panels to prefer:
- `endpoint` not `route`
- `model_family` not `model_id`
- separate panels for TTFT and stream_duration

Thomas Baird: dedicated tier question: do we ever need `customer_id` in shared metrics?

Aisha Bello: not in shared. Dedicated SLOs are per-customer but we should compute in the customer’s restricted namespace. For central views, roll up to “Dedicated aggregate” without identifiers.

Logan Wright: +1. We can do separate M3 tenant/namespace for Dedicated-per-customer metrics with tighter retention + access controls.

Allison Grant: action items?

Thomas Baird:
- [Amara] switch gateway route -> `endpoint` template + remove raw path label
- [Logan/Thomas] draft “cardinality budget + labeling rules” (Drive doc exists, will update) + post in #eng-platform and #eng-sre
- [Sergio] adjust SLO dashboard queries to stop selecting high-card dims by default
- [Nadia/Caleb] propose sampling strategy for per-model tail drilldown (traces/logs) and how it ties into SLO job

Sergio Costa: :thumbsup: also can we add a hard cap in alerts? e.g., if series count for a metric jumps >2x day-over-day, page telemetry/oncall.

Logan Wright: we can alert on cardinality anomalies, but paging might be too aggressive. Maybe ticket + Slack ping first.

Thomas Baird: agree. we’ll start with a daily report + threshold-based warning in #eng-infra.

Caleb Johnson: (small note) if we do allowlists pushed daily, ensure services handle “config missing” safely. don’t block metrics emission.

Nadia Rahman: also: `status` label should be class not code. We don’t need 200/201/204 split.

Amara Diallo: ack. I’ll switch to `status_class`.

Thomas Baird: cool. I’ll post a summary in the cardinality proposal doc and link here.

Thomas Baird: link: https://drive.google.com/.../cardinality-budget-and-labeling-proposal (WIP) — comments welcome.

Sergio Costa reacted with :eyes:

Logan Wright reacted with :thumbsup:

Allison Grant: thanks all. this is exactly the kind of pre-work that saves us later when SLO dashboards go global.
